Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verses 1–2:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Jathiya (The Kneeling)

It is Meccan,

except for one verse, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not hope for the Days of Allah﴾. It was revealed in Medina. It is also said that the whole surah is Meccan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. His saying: ﴿Ha Mim﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ is its predicate (khabar). His saying: ﴿from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ means: the Dominant over affairs (al-Ghalib), the Just in judgments (al-'Adl fi al-ahkam).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verses 1–2:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Jathiya (The Kneeling)

It is Meccan,

except for one verse, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not hope for the Days of Allah﴾. It was revealed in Medina. It is also said that the whole surah is Meccan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. His saying: ﴿Ha Mim﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ is its predicate (khabar). His saying: ﴿from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ means: the Dominant over affairs (al-Ghalib), the Just in judgments (al-'Adl fi al-ahkam).

Almighty God's words: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾, that is: proofs and lessons. This refers to His raising them up without pillars, and to what He created in them of the sun, the moon and the stars, and to His spreading out the earth and making it firm with its inhabitants, and to the mountains He set upon it and the rivers He caused to flow in it, and the trees He created, and other things. His words ﴿for the believers﴾ mean: for those who affirm the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And in your creation﴾, i.e., in your creation from dust, then from a drop of semen (nutfah).

And His saying: ﴿and what He spreads abroad of living creatures﴾, i.e., what is dispersed upon the earth of living creatures. The dabbah (a creature that crawls, i.e., any animal that moves upon the earth) is every living creature that crawls upon the earth.

And His saying: ﴿signs﴾. It has been read as "āyātun" with both the nominative and the genitive. As for the one who reads it in the genitive (āyātin), its meaning is: Indeed in the heavens and indeed in your creation are signs. As for the one who reads it in the nominative (āyātun), it is on the basis of a new beginning (ibtida' wa-isti'naf).

And His saying: ﴿for a people who are certain﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Faith (al-iman) is certainty (al-yaqin) in its entirety."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 5:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾. The meaning of ikhtilaf (alternation, i.e. difference and succession) is increase and decrease, and coming and going.

And His saying: ﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of provision﴾, meaning: the rain. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: The rain descends, and in it is the seed, so it enters the earth and then emerges from it.

And His saying: ﴿and gives life thereby to the earth after its death﴾. We have already mentioned this.

﴿And the turning of the winds﴾. Its meaning: sometimes from the south, and sometimes from the north, and sometimes as mercy, and sometimes as punishment.

And His saying: ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾, meaning: who reason about the signs. And in a report it is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The wind is from the Spirit of Allah; it comes sometimes with punishment and sometimes with mercy. So do not curse it, but when it comes, ask Allah for its good and seek refuge in Allah from its evil."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. Then in what message after Allah and His verses will they believe?﴾ That is, they will affirm (yuṣaddiqūn). The real meaning is that if they do not believe in this Book, then in what Book after it will they believe? There is no Book after this Book.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾. In the tafsir it is said that "woe" (wayl) is a valley in Hell into which the disbeliever plunges for seventy autumns before reaching its bottom. As for His words ﴿every sinful liar﴾, it means: a great liar, an evil transgressor.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 8:

The words of the Most High: ﴿He hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then he persists in arrogance﴾. That is: he persists in disbelief, turning away from the truth with the turning-away of the arrogant. And iṣrār (persistence) is to hold firmly to a thing with a sound resolve.

And His words: ﴿as if he had not heard them﴾. That is: as if he had not heard the verses.

And His words: ﴿so give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾. That is: painful, causing pain.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when he learns anything of Our verses, he takes it in mockery.﴾ The verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kalada. He used to say about the Qur'an that it is "the fables of the ancients" (asatir al-awwalin), and it is like the story of Rustam and Isfandiyar. He would say this by way of mockery.

And His saying: ﴿For them there is a humiliating punishment.﴾ We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 10:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Hell is before them﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "Hell is before them" (min qudamihim jahannam).

And His words: ﴿Nor will what they earned avail them at all﴾. Some of the people of tafsir said: the verse concerns 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and his earning was his jihad alongside the Messenger, his fasting, his prayer, and his compassion toward the Companions of the Prophet. As for His words ﴿will avail﴾, it means: will not repel [punishment]. And it did not repel it because he was a hypocrite who showed Islam with his tongue while believing in disbelief. Most of the scholars hold that this verse also concerns al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and this is the preferred view, because the surah is Meccan, and his earning was what he did of good according to his own claim.

His words: ﴿Nor what they took as protectors besides Allah﴾, meaning: the idols.

His words: ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾: its meaning is apparent.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This is guidance﴾, meaning: the Qur'an is guidance for creation.

And His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them is a painful punishment﴾, meaning: a punishment from Hell, painful.

Allah's words: ﴿It is Allah who subjected the sea to you, that the ships may sail upon it by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ — meaning: of His provision (rizq).

And His words: ﴿And perhaps you will be grateful﴾. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Gratitude (shukr) is obligatory upon every Muslim, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾. So He provided for His servants so that they would give thanks to Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 13:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ mean: He made them subservient (dhalala). The meaning of subjugation (taskhir) and making subservient (tadhlil) is that He created them in a manner by which the servants benefit from them, and benefit from the heavens and the earth is well known.

As for His words ﴿all of it from Him﴾, al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: it is a blessing and a mercy from Him. ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "From Him is the light, and from Him are the sun, the moon and the stars." And in some reports: a man came to ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar and said: "From what did God create creation?" He said: "From light, darkness and wind." He said: "From what were light, darkness and wind created?" He said: "I do not know." So he came to Ibn ʿAbbas and asked about the first (question), and he mentioned the same as Ibn ʿUmar had mentioned. He asked him about the second, and he recited the words of the Exalted: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾, meaning: from His creating, as if He said to it: "Be," and it was. It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he read "minnah" (as a blessing), meaning: that which He subjected is a blessing from God.

As for His words ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾, meaning: who ponder.

And in a report: "Reflect upon the creation, and do not reflect upon the Creator."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 14:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾. Al-Dahhak and Abu Salih mentioned that the Prophet and his Companions alighted at a water source at al-Muraysi', so Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul sent his slave boy to bring them water. The boy was delayed, and when he returned, [Abdullah] said to him: "What delayed you?" He said: "The slave of Umar came and sat at the mouth of the well, and prevented the people until he filled the waterskins of the Prophet, the waterskin of Abu Bakr, and the waterskin of his master." Abdullah ibn Ubayy became angry when he heard that, and said: "Our situation and that of Muhammad is only as it is said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.'" Then he said: "If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it." When this reached Umar, he came with his sword unsheathed, intending to strike Abdullah ibn Ubayy with it, and he sought the Prophet's permission for that. So Allah the Most High sent down His words: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾. This is according to the view we mentioned that the verse was revealed in Medina. Others said: a man among the disbelievers insulted Umar in Mecca, and he resolved to lash out at him; so Allah the Most High sent down this verse.

His words: ﴿those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾ mean: those who do not ask Allah for His blessings; the meaning is that they do not acknowledge that blessings come from Allah. It was also said: "do not expect the Days of Allah" means: they do not fear the punishments and vengeance of Allah. It was also said: they do not hope for reward and do not fear punishment.

His words: ﴿that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾ mean: on the Day of Resurrection. It is also said: that Allah Himself may be the one who requites and avenges upon them, not you.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self; and whoever does evil, it is against it.﴾ That is, the benefit of that returns to him.

And His words: ﴿And whoever does evil, it is against it.﴾ That is, the burden of that falls upon him.

And His words: ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾ That is, you will be brought back.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We gave the Children of Israel the Book﴾, meaning: the Torah.

And His saying: ﴿and the judgment and prophethood﴾, meaning: the knowledge and prophethood.

And His saying: ﴿and We provided them with good things﴾, meaning: the lawful (ḥalāl), which are the manna and the quail and other than that.

And His saying: ﴿and We preferred them over the worlds﴾, meaning: over the worlds of their time.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 17:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the affair﴾, meaning: clear indications. It is also said: "clear proofs concerning the affair" are that which points them to the affair of Muhammad.

And His words: ﴿And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them﴾, meaning: they did not differ concerning the truth except after knowledge of the truth had come to them.

And His words: ﴿out of mutual envy among themselves﴾, meaning: out of envy, injustice, and obstinate opposition to the truth.

And His words: ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them﴾, its apparent meaning is clear, up to the end of the verse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 18:

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿Then We placed you on a path (shari'ah) of the affair﴾ means: a clear way. It is also said: "on a clear matter." The shir'ah (law, path) is the madhhab (way, doctrine) and the millah (religion), and likewise the shari'ah.

His words: ﴿so follow it﴾ mean: follow the shari'ah that has come to you from Allah the Exalted.

His words: ﴿and do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾: in the exegesis, it is that the polytheists used to say, "O Muhammad, return to the religion of your fathers, for it is better than the religion you have brought."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 19:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they will not avail you anything against Allah﴾ means: they will not repel from you anything that Allah intends for you if you follow their desires.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾ means: some of them love one another.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is the Ally of the righteous﴾ means: He loves the righteous and protects them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 20:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿This is insights for mankind﴾, meaning: this which We have sent down to you is insights for mankind, that is, proofs by which people see clearly.

And His saying: ﴿and guidance and mercy for a people who have certainty﴾, meaning: who know.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds (ijtarahu al-sayyi'at) think...﴾ That is, those who acquired (iktasabu) the evil deeds. "Evil deeds" (al-sayyi'at) are what is deemed ugly by the Sharia, and "good deeds" (al-hasanat) are what is deemed good by the Sharia.

And His saying: ﴿that We would make them like those who believed and did righteous deeds?﴾ That is, in entering Paradise and in the bounty given to the people of faith. Apparently the verse concerns the disbelievers, although its wording is general.

And His saying: ﴿Their living and their dying are alike.﴾ It was also read "sawa'" in the accusative. Whoever reads it in the nominative (raf'), its meaning is that the disbeliever's living and dying are alike, that is, he lives as a disbeliever and dies as a disbeliever.

In a report: "A man dies upon what he lived upon, and is resurrected upon what he died upon."

As for the reading in the accusative, it is in a position of equality, so it takes the accusative for this reason. It is also said that its meaning is: "Did they suppose that We would make them and the believers equal in living and dying?" meaning: they are not equal.

And His saying: ﴿Evil is their judgment.﴾ That is, wretched is what they judge for themselves. In the exegesis it is related that they used to say to the believers: "If you enter Paradise, we will be with you, and if we enter the Fire, you will be with us."

In some reports from Masruq ibn al-Ajda' who said: I came to Mecca and entered the Sacred Mosque, and it was said to me: "This is the station of your brother Tamim al-Dari." He would pray through the night until morning, bowing, prostrating, and weeping, and reciting this verse: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think...﴾ and would not go beyond it.

"His Exalted saying: ﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged﴾. That is: nothing will be diminished from their rights."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 23:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: One of them would worship a thing, and when he saw something better than it, he would cast aside the first and take the second and worship it. Qatadah said regarding the meaning of the verse: He does not desire anything without mounting it, so he worships his desire. It was also said: "Takes his desire as his god" means he obeys his desire and submits to it, just as a slave submits to the one he worships. And it is established that he (ﷺ) said: "Wretched is the slave of the dinar, wretched is the slave of the dirham, wretched is the slave of the embroidered cloak."

In some reports it is said that he [said]: "Nothing under the sky is worshipped that is more hateful to Allah than desire."

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah has misguided him knowingly﴾, i.e., according to what He decreed for him in His prior knowledge. This is a refutation of the Qadariyyah (the Qadariyyah, a early school who denied divine predestination). They have interpreted this and said: the meaning of His saying ﴿And Allah has misguided him﴾ is that He found him astray, or named him astray. This is a false interpretation, because the Arabs do not say "So-and-so did such-and-such" when they mean that they found him to be so.

As for His saying: ﴿And has sealed over his hearing﴾, i.e., He sealed his hearing, so that he does not hear the truth.

As for His saying: ﴿and his heart﴾, i.e., and He sealed his heart, so that it does not accept the truth.

As for His saying: ﴿and has put over his sight a covering﴾, i.e., a veil, so that he does not see the truth.

As for His saying: ﴿So who will guide him after Allah?﴾, meaning: if Allah does not guide him, then who will guide him after Allah?

As for His saying: ﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾, i.e., will you not then take warning?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "There is nothing but our worldly life; we die and we live."﴾ Concerning this there are several opinions. The first: it is inverted in order (al-taqdim wa'l-ta'khir), and its meaning is "we live and we die." Thus Ibn Mas'ud recited it.

The second opinion: "we die and we live" means that some of us die and some of us live. There are two further opinions regarding this: the first, which is the third opinion: "we die and we live" meaning we ourselves die and our children live; the fourth opinion: that He created us dead and then gave us life.

And His saying: ﴿And nothing destroys us except time (al-dahr).﴾ Qatadah said: "[It is] the days and nights." And it is said: "Nothing destroys us except time," meaning: except death. The poet said:

(Does the one who fears what fate brings and its uncertainty grieve? Time does not blame the one who laments.)

That is, death. It is also said: "And nothing destroys us except time," meaning: the length of life. And it has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Do not revile time, for God is time."

The Shaykh, the Imam, may God be pleased with him, said: Abu'l-Husayn al-Naqqur informed us of this; Abu'l-Qasim ibn Hababa informed us; al-Baghawi, who is the son of the daughter of Mani' and whose name is Abdullah ibn Muhammad, Abu'l-Qasim, informed us; Hudbah ibn Khalid informed us; Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, the report.

Al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God, exalted is He, says: I was asked for a loan by the son of Adam, but he did not lend to Me; he reviles Me, while he does not know it, and he says: 'Oh time! Oh time!'" And in another narration: "O misfortune of time!" and "I am time."

And in a third narration from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "God, exalted is He, says: The son of Adam harms Me; he reviles time, and I am time. I direct the affair; I alternate the night and the day."

Regarding the meaning of the report there are three aspects. The first: its meaning is, "Do not revile time, for God is time," i.e., the Creator of time.

The second aspect: "Do not revile time, for it is I who am the doer of things." They used to attribute the action to time and revile it, so "God is time" means that God is the doer of things, not time; and this is a well-founded opinion.

The third aspect: they used to believe in the eternity of time, and that nothing remains with time's permanence; so He said, "Do not revile time," meaning: do not revile those who believe that it is the everlasting; "for God is time," meaning: God is the everlasting, with the everlastingness of eternity, according to what they believed about time.

And His saying: ﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾ That is: they said what they said out of conjecture and doubt, not from knowledge and certainty.

**The saying of God Most High:** ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is nothing but that they say, "Bring us our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾

And we have already explained the saying of Abu Jahl concerning this.

The Most High said: ﴿Say, "It is Allah who gives you life, then causes you to die, then gathers you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt; but most people do not know."﴾ Meaning: they do not know the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 27:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the Hour will be established on the Day when the Hour is established﴾, meaning: the Resurrection (al-qiyamah).

And His saying: ﴿On that Day the falsifiers will lose﴾, meaning: the disbelievers will perish.

**The words of the Exalted: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling﴾.** On this there are several views. The first is that it means *mustawfizin* (sitting on the knees, ready to rise), that is, sitting on their knees. Sufyan al-Thawri said: "The *mustawfiz* is one from whom only his two knees and the tips of his toes touch the ground." The second view is that *jathiyah* means gathered together. The third view is that *jathiyah* means submissive and humbled. It was also said that this is the dialect of Quraysh. The first view is the preferred and well-known one, and from it comes the expression: "So-and-so knelt before the judge awaiting his ruling." It is reported from Salman al-Farisi that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection there is an hour that equals ten years of the years of this world, in which people will fall down and kneel on their knees, until even Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful, will say: 'My own self, my own self; I ask nothing but for myself.'" It is also said that the meaning of ﴿you will see every nation of a messenger kneeling﴾ is that every person is kneeling, since *ummah* can be used to mean a single individual. And it is said that its meaning is: every nation of a messenger is kneeling. And Allah knows best.

**His words: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record﴾.** Its meaning is: to the reading of its record.

**The words of the Exalted: ﴿Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do﴾.** Its meaning is apparent.

This is the commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 45, verse 29:

Allah's statement: ﴿This Book of Ours speaks against you with the truth﴾ means: it manifests what you have done, with the truth.

And His statement: ﴿Indeed, We were having (what you used to do) copied﴾ (nastansikh, "to copy/transcribe") has several interpretations. One: "We had your deeds dictated" (nastaktib), meaning: We ordered the scribes to write down and preserve your deeds. The second view: "We copied what you used to do," meaning: We took a copy of what the angels had recorded against you. The third view, which is the well-known one and is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah commands the angels to take a copy from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) of what the servant does during his day and night. Then they write down what the servant has done, and then they compare what they wrote against the servant with what they copied from the Preserved Tablet, so that the two are identical, with neither addition nor omission in it. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Consider: is copying anything other than copying from an original?"

The Exalted's saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy﴾, meaning: into His Garden. And His saying: (That is the manifest triumph), meaning: the clear one.

"As for those who disbelieved: 'Were not My verses recited to you?'" That is, it will be said to them: "Were not My verses recited to you?" Meaning: "Were not My verses recited to you?"

His words "but you were arrogant" mean: you sought greatness and majesty by abandoning monotheism (tawhid). Every disbeliever is arrogant, and every believer is humble.

His words "and you were criminals" mean: possessors of sin (jurm).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: (When it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt about it"), meaning: there is no doubt in it.

And His saying: (You said, "We do not know what the Hour is; we only think it is a mere assumption"), meaning: we assume that you are a liar, and we assume that you are truthful, and there is no proof with us of your truthfulness, nor that what you have said is true.

And His saying: ﴿And we are not certain﴾, meaning: certain.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there will become apparent to them the evils of what they did﴾, meaning: there will become apparent to them the evils of what they did.

And His saying: ﴿And there will surround them that which they used to mock at﴾, meaning: there will descend upon them and encompass them the recompense of that which they used to mock at. It is said in the tafsir: when the Day of Resurrection comes, He will call out to one of them, saying, "O so-and-so, come and take your light," and He will call out to another, saying, "Go away, for there is no light for you."

And it is said: "Today We shall forget you" (Quran 45:34), i.e., We shall abandon you, and its meaning is: We shall abandon you from mercy and the bestowal of reward. It is also said its meaning is: We shall abandon you in the punishment, so We will not bring you out of it as We bring out the believers.

And His saying: "As you forgot the meeting of this your day" (Quran 45:34), i.e., as you abandoned the work for this your day.

And His saying: "And your abode is the Fire, and you have no helpers" (Quran 45:34), i.e., none who can prevent Our punishment from you.

That is, the Qur'an says: ﴿This is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the worldly life deceived you. So today they shall not be brought out of it﴾, meaning out of the Fire.

﴿Nor shall they be allowed to make amends﴾, meaning they will not return or be restored to the well-being they had been in. It is also said: they will ask to be relieved, but they will not be relieved. It is also said: ﴿nor shall they be allowed to make amends﴾ means they will not be given al-'utba (ʿutbā), which is the seeking of their pleasure and their desire.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 45, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Him belongs the grandeur in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the magnificence and the loftiness. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah, exalted is He, says: Greatness is My cloak, and Majesty is My waistwrap; whoever disputes with Me over either of them, I will cast him into Hell."

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, meaning: the Mighty in His retribution, the Wise in His governance. And Allah knows best.
